key_insight: For ZrO₂, accurate relative polymorph energies and phonon spectra without systematic softening identify pretrained force fields more likely to reproduce the correct phase-transition sequence.
engineering_relevance: These ground-state checks offer practical screening criteria before using pretrained force fields for lower-cost finite-temperature phase-transition simulations.
method: Benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields on ZrO₂.
Compare phonon dispersions and relative polymorph energies with matched density functional theory references.
Test heating-induced phase sequences using variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics.
evidence_signal: Four of ten models reproduced monoclinic–tetragonal–cubic transitions; three with orthorhombic–tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom introduced an orthorhombic intermediate, while ORB-based models failed to sustain stable variable-cell dynamics.
watch_item: The proposed approximately 6 meV/atom energy-agreement criterion and phonon-screening guidance were established for ZrO₂; transferability to other materials remains untested here.
paper_title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
